title: A Waymo robotaxi is pulled over in San Francisco's Richmond District after the company detects a firearm violation; police find a loaded AR-style 'ghost gun' and book two juveniles
summary: LA Times (12 Sep 2026): before 4 a.m. on 3 Sep Waymo pulled a robotaxi over in the Richmond District after detecting a firearm violation; SFPD found a loaded ghost gun and booked two minors.
account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District after detecting 'a violation of our terms of service involving a firearm', alerted emergency services and 'cooperated fully' with police, a Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September). The San Francisco Police Department said officers made a 'high-risk vehicle stop', detained the two juvenile passengers and found a loaded AR-style assault rifle, suspected marijuana and mace spray; the two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes SFPD spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an 'AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun' and says the boy and girl were booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges; the California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. No source says how the firearm was detected; The Independent and Xataka both say this is unclear.
purpose: The Waymo Driver is built to provide driverless rides; the service's rider rules prohibit weapons, and Xataka says interior cameras record rides so that the company can check compliance and respond to emergencies. Pulling over and calling police on a firearm violation is that safeguard working, not a driving function.
system: Waymo driverless ride-hail vehicle (Waymo Driver) with the company's in-ride monitoring and terms-of-service enforcement
taxonomy_note: No taxonomy type covers public safety; chosen because a company safeguard handed San Francisco police a stop, a seizure and two arrests without any officer-initiated investigation, as in the earlier policing records. Protective response rather than harm prevented because no source says the rifle was about to be used. The Monitor says the vehicle's AI detected the firearm; no source describes the detection mechanism.

ratings.reason: SFPD took a loaded AR-style ghost gun, suspected marijuana and mace from two juveniles and booked both on firearm-possession charges after the company's alert, per the Los Angeles Times and The Independent.
A loaded unserialized rifle was taken out of circulation and two minors were charged; no report shows a harm that was about to occur, so the public benefit is the seizure itself.

ai_role.statement: What the system did is established only at the level of the company: Waymo says it detected a terms-of-service violation involving a firearm, pulled the driverless car over and alerted emergency services. The Independent says it is not clear how the firearm was detected, and Xataka says Waymo has not explained whether detection was automatic or human. The Monitor's statement that the vehicle's AI detected the gun is not supported by any fetched source; the driverless car's ability to stop on command is the only system function the accounts describe.
